WITH per_order_avgs AS (
  SELECT 
    ordersmark,
    AVG(CASE WHEN fillcount > 0 THEN fillcount ELSE NULL END) as avg_fillcount
  FROM orderexecutions
  GROUP BY ordersmark
),
benchmark1 AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_fillcount) as bench1_value
  FROM per_order_avgs
),
above_bench1 AS (
  SELECT 
    p.ordersmark,
    p.avg_fillcount,
    (p.avg_fillcount - b.bench1_value) as first_excess
  FROM per_order_avgs p
  CROSS JOIN benchmark1 b
  WHERE p.avg_fillcount > b.bench1_value
),
benchmark2 AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_fillcount) as bench2_value
  FROM above_bench1
),
above_bench2 AS (
  SELECT 
    a.ordersmark,
    a.avg_fillcount,
    a.first_excess,
    (a.avg_fillcount - b.bench2_value) as second_excess
  FROM above_bench1 a
  CROSS JOIN benchmark2 b
  WHERE a.avg_fillcount > b.bench2_value
)
SELECT 
  AVG(avg_fillcount) as avg_fillcount,
  AVG(first_excess) as avg_first_excess,
  AVG(second_excess) as avg_second_excess
FROM above_bench2

assumptions.assumption: Zero-valued fillcount (0, 0.0000, etc.) and NULL fillcount entries are excluded entirely from per-order average calculations, not treated as zero contributors.
NULL ordersmark values are grouped together as a single cohort and processed identically to non-null ordersmark groups.
All three final summary statistics (avg_fillcount, avg_first_excess, avg_second_excess) are computed only from the orders that remain after the second threshold filter (those exceeding benchmark2).

alternatives.interpretation: "Average per-order fill quantity" could mean the arithmetic mean of *all* fillcount values in the final orders (treating each execution equally), rather than the average of per-order averages (treating each order equally regardless of execution count). This would yield different results if orders have unequal execution counts.

WITH per_order_avgs AS (
  SELECT 
    ordersmark,
    AVG(CASE WHEN fillcount > 0 THEN fillcount ELSE NULL END) as avg_fillcount
  FROM orderexecutions
  GROUP BY ordersmark
),
benchmark1 AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_fillcount) as bench1_value
  FROM per_order_avgs
),
above_bench1 AS (
  SELECT 
    p.ordersmark,
    p.avg_fillcount,
    (p.avg_fillcount - b.bench1_value) as first_excess
  FROM per_order_avgs p
  CROSS JOIN benchmark1 b
  WHERE p.avg_fillcount > b.bench1_value
),
benchmark2 AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_fillcount) as bench2_value
  FROM above_bench1
),
above_bench2_orders AS (
  SELECT 
    a.ordersmark,
    a.avg_fillcount,
    a.first_excess,
    (a.avg_fillcount - b.bench2_value) as second_excess
  FROM above_bench1 a
  CROSS JOIN benchmark2 b
  WHERE a.avg_fillcount > b.bench2_value
),
final_execs AS (
  SELECT 
    o.fillcount,
    ab.first_excess,
    ab.second_excess
  FROM orderexecutions o
  JOIN above_bench2_orders ab ON o.ordersmark = ab.ordersmark
  WHERE o.fillcount > 0
)
SELECT 
  AVG(fillcount) as avg_fillcount,
  AVG(first_excess) as avg_first_excess,
  AVG(second_excess) as avg_second_excess
FROM final_execs
